claims.statement: The Vitest unit tier is configured in the test block of vite.config.ts with environment jsdom, globals true, include src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}, and an exclude list that explicitly drops *.integration.test.{ts,tsx} (the exclude replaces Vite's default list rather than appending, so the usual node_modules/dist/etc. entries are repeated alongside it).
The unit tier runs via `npm test` (`vitest run`) and `npm run test:watch` (`vitest`), as defined in package.json scripts.

The integration tier uses a standalone config (vitest.integration.config.ts) rather than mergeConfig over vite.config.ts, because Vite's mergeConfig concatenates array fields like test.include instead of replacing them, which would silently pull the ~90 unit test files into the integration run too.
The integration tier runs via `npm run test:integration` (`vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts`) and includes only src/test/integration/**/*.integration.test.tsx.

Integration tests mock getPlatform() to inject a fake PlatformAdapter at that single seam — the same interface TauriAdapter and the inert createUnsupportedAdapter implement — which makes the whole app run under jsdom without a real Tauri runtime. The fakes do real fs work (saveProject/openProject write and read the scratch repo), so git status/diff see genuine content.

Each integration test spins up a real scratch git repository per test (mkdtempSync, git init, initial commit) and wires a fake GitPlatform whose status/commit/beginPull/etc. shell out to the real git binary against that directory, so merge/pull/push/branch-switch/discard flows run against genuine git rather than a stub.

Integration tests render the real React components with React Testing Library (render/screen/userEvent) and drive them with real clicks/typing/DOM events, not direct store calls; because jsdom performs no real layout they stub getBoundingClientRect/Range.getClientRects/ResizeObserver and mock react-pdf, but everything above that (selection capture, mark creation, the comment popover, annotation form, Git panel) is the genuine component code.

Integration tests verify outcomes independently of the app by reading the scratch repo directly (e.g. git log -1 --format=%s, git show HEAD:project.json), so a green test proves a real commit landed rather than just that the store claims it did.

The integration suite in src/test/integration/ covers annotationWorkflow (schema authoring, PDF annotation, git commit), consolidationAndMerge (multi-reviewer consolidation and a real merge conflict), branchSwitch (stash-carry-over field-level conflict), pull (real git pull against a bare origin diverged by a second clone), discard (writeWorking not commit), pdfReadingPosition, screeningImport, fetchPolicy (background-fetch safety guard against a repo whose own config names a fetch command — core.sshCommand/credential.helper/include.path, tested against real git config --get-regexp), stashOps (pushStash/restoreStash/dropStash/branchFromStash and the branch-switch carry-over — a stash that no longer fits rolls all the way back, never leaving conflict markers), annotationSplit (splitting a shared annotations folder so git sees renames), and gitScenarios (the scenario rig: every scenario builds and holds what its README entry promises).

scripts/ci.sh is the provider-agnostic single source of truth for whether the app builds and passes its checks; CI providers only check out the code, provide a Node toolchain, and run this script, so the same checks run locally with ./scripts/ci.sh. It runs steps in order with set -euo pipefail: dependency install (npm ci with an npm install fallback, skippable with SKIP_INSTALL=1), typecheck (tsc), wiki link check (check:wiki), unit tests (npm test), integration tests (npm run test:integration), and build (vite build).

ci.yml has four jobs that all gate every push (to main and release/**) and every pull request (both paths-ignoring technical-report/**): build (ubuntu, Node 24) runs scripts/ci.sh; rust runs cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy -D warnings (tests are not run here); tauri-build runs cargo test per OS across a 5-OS matrix plus the installer build and the headless probe run; tauri-e2e runs the probe through tauri-driver on ubuntu-24.04 and windows-latest (no macOS, which tauri-driver does not support). There is deliberately no push-on-every-branch trigger to avoid double-building branches with open PRs.

Pure model tests in src/model/model.test.ts cover schema resolution (defaults, path ids, duplicate sibling names, enum options, max<min rejection, required defaults, and visibleIf conditional-visibility resolution — bare-name, absolute-path, nested all/any groups, equals filtering, cross-branch/ancestor reads), isFieldVisible (fail-open semantics, per-instance repeatable reads), normalizeTree/pruneTree/canAdd/canRemove, loadProject input validation (ProjectLoadError), loadProject→serializeProject round-trip, Paper.finished (a human declaration not derived), Paper.aiUsage (AI-use disclosure), config.ai (an opt-in: disabled when absent, enabled only by an explicit true, written only when enabled), config.aiSeat, config.reviewers/Paper.reviews (multi-reviewer skeleton, per-reviewer normalization, deterministic serialization), Paper.equal, screening, Project.provenance/protocol/schemaInfo (degrade field-by-field rather than all-or-nothing), and a regression for hand-edited primitive instances the loader must adopt as values rather than crash on — with fixtures built through the real load path (loadProject/serializeProject) so inputs are exactly as schema-normalized as a real file would be.

Store tests (src/state/store.*.test.ts) mock the platform seam at getPlatform() with a fake PlatformAdapter, use a beforeEach that loads a known project via loadFromText, and cover annotation lifecycle, undo/redo (coalescing consecutive same-field edits into one step, a new edit clearing the redo stack), marks, reading position, reviewer seats, save/save-as, finished flags, and AI-suggestion application (never overwriting the reviewer, one undo step per run, a no-op run leaving no trace).

gitStore.test.ts stubs the full GitPlatform shape and drives runPull's orchestration (dirty guard, pull classification, parse boundary, merge, resolution dialog) through each branch via beginPullResult/finishPullResult, exercising exactly the branch each test means to test.

merge.test.ts in src/git builds base/ours/theirs fixtures through loadProject (the real load path, not hand-assembled Project objects) so each side is exactly as schema-normalized and empty-skeleton-shaped as a file mergeProjects' caller would actually hand it, covering merge3/mergeProjects/applyResolutions/conflictId over repeatable findings and paper-meta fields.

ref.test.ts covers refProblem, the ref/path safety guard that refuses empty refs, option-like refs (--upload-pack=…), control characters, revision syntax (main^, main~1, main:path, main@{1}), and everything git check-ref-format forbids (spaces, ? * [ \ , leading/trailing/double slashes, trailing dot, .lock) at any path level.

Component tests come in two shapes: src/components/*.test.ts files test pure helper functions extracted from components directly without rendering (PaperList's paperIsMarkedDone/paperMetadataHaystack, GitDialog's mixedDiscardConfirmMessage and isProjectOwnPath, PdfViewer's destinationPoint/markVerticallyVisible/dedupeOverlappingRects, PapersEditor's duplicatePaperIds, Toolbar's gitButtonState/aiButtonState), while the *.test.tsx files render real components under jsdom with React Testing Library; the multi-step, multi-component workflows live in the integration suite.

paperIsMarkedDone (PaperList) decides the paper-list status dot; in Consolidation the dot must mean 'every numbered reviewer has answered', read from paper.reviews, not 'does paper.annotations have anything' — because adoptUnanimousValues fills paper.annotations just from opening the paper, making annotations presence no longer a signal the consolidator produced. The regression test pins a paper with full annotations and a missing reviewer tree as not done.

mixedDiscardConfirmMessage (GitDialog) warns before a commit silently reverts or deletes a Discard row; a PaperChange marked Discard deletes the paper and all its annotation files (consolidated.json, every reviewer-<n>.json), so it is named as '1 paper' (with 'deleted') rather than the badly-underselling '1 field ... reverted', and discard-only mode suppresses this warning because it has its own separate confirm.

Because jsdom has no layout engine, the integration tests give every element a fixed non-zero getBoundingClientRect (800x1000) and Range.getClientRects a 100x20 rect, which is enough for PdfViewer's own width>1 && height>1 filter (rectsForPageRange) to keep selection rects so the real selection-to-highlight code path produces a real mark; ResizeObserver and the CSS Custom Highlight API (used for in-PDF search) are stubbed as unused.

PlatformAdapter (src/platform/adapter.ts) is the platform abstraction for file I/O, PDF loading, LLM calls, git access and self-update; TauriAdapter is its only live implementation (driving the Tauri bridge), while createUnsupportedAdapter is an inert Proxy stand-in that refuses every action now that the browser/web build is discontinued. It exposes openProject/saveProject/rebasePdfPaths/getPdfSource plus getGit(), and is the single seam both unit and integration tests mock with a fake implementation.

SaiLoR is checked in four deliberately separated test layers, each owning the class of bug the layer below it structurally cannot see: Vitest unit tests (npm test, the fast per-PR tier), a jsdom integration suite that mocks the platform seam and spins up real scratch git repos (npm run test:integration, slower and excluded from the default run but part of CI), Rust unit tests inline in every src-tauri/src module (cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml), and the tauri-driver e2e probe (a minimal e2e/ page built with the probe cargo feature and driven by node --test e2e/probe.test.mjs).

The Rust test layer lives inline: every module in src-tauri/src/ except main.rs has a #[cfg(test)] mod tests block. git.rs (the largest module) pins the shell's security and parsing gates — rel_path_problem/validate_git_url/validate_clone_path and ref_problem vectors shared with the renderer's src/git tests, the porcelain/log/stash-list/annotation-authors parsers, own-annotation-path matching, merge-blocking and repo-setup rules — and then runs the real command surface against real scratch repositories (info/status/commit with the detached-HEAD refusal, pull fast-forward/merge/conflict-elsewhere through a clone pair, stash push/restore/drop, branch-switch begin/abort/finish, commit_partial/write_working, discard rules, and a unix symlink-escape check).

protocol.rs's Rust unit tests pin the slr-file:// scheme's security and serving behaviour: ../secret.pdf, pdfs/../../secret.pdf and an absolute path all return 403, a missing file 404, and a session with no project open says so — plus single byte-range serving (206 with Content-Range, 416 for unsatisfiable, malformed/multi-range treated as whole-file), the OPTIONS preflight allowing Range, and form-encoded plus-as-space query parsing. webfetch.rs pins the SSRF guard's blocked-address/blocked-hostname vectors, update.rs asserts the updater feed is the fixed HTTPS GitHub endpoint with requireSignedVersion true read from tauri.conf.json itself, and project.rs pins that save refuses a path the session never opened (the 'Refusing to save' guard).

CI runs the Rust tests per OS rather than once: the tauri-build matrix job (macos-15, macos-26, windows-latest, ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-24.04) runs cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml before building the installer bundle, and the separate rust lint job gates cargo fmt --check plus cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features with -D warnings. Locally the same two checks are make test-rust and make lint.

The e2e layer is the probe app, replacing the Electron-era Playwright specs: a minimal React page (e2e/index.html + e2e/main.tsx, sharing the app's pdf.js worker setup via src/platform/pdfjs) that is not the real app, built into the real binary and driven through tauri-driver by e2e/probe.test.mjs (node:test). It is the one layer that proves, in a real system WebView, that the shell serves the embedded frontend, that slr-file:// refuses a traversal with 403, and that pdf.js actually renders a real PDF.

make probe builds the probe with `npx tauri build --no-bundle --features probe --config src-tauri/tauri.probe.conf.json`. tauri.probe.conf.json swaps the frontend to vite.probe.config.ts (root e2e/, outDir ../dist-probe, dev port 5199), so the binary embeds the probe page instead of the real app. The probe cargo feature adds exactly two commands — probe_auto (open $SAILOR_PROBE_PROJECT without a dialog and register its directory so slr-file:// can resolve PDFs) and probe_report (append a line to $SAILOR_PROBE_REPORT) — and is never enabled in a release build.

The probe page, on mount, calls probe_auto, lists the project's PDFs, then fetches ../package.json and nope.pdf through the custom scheme logging `probe <rel> -> <status>` for each (the traversal must come back 403), renders the first paper's PDF with react-pdf logging `PDF OK pages=N` then `RENDER OK` on render success, and mirrors every line into the in-page #log element and via probe_report into the report file. The scheme base is http://slr-file.localhost on Windows and slr-file://localhost elsewhere.

probe.test.mjs drives the built probe binary through tauri-driver's WebDriver endpoint on 127.0.0.1:4444 with plain fetch: it spawns tauri-driver with SAILOR_PROBE_PROJECT set, creates a session whose application is the probe binary, polls document #log via execute/sync for up to 60 seconds, and asserts the log matches both /RENDER OK/ and /-> 403/. In CI the tauri-e2e job runs it on ubuntu-24.04 (under xvfb-run) and windows-latest (at medium integrity via gsudo, with an msedgedriver matched to the installed WebView2, because WebView2 ignores the driver's browser arguments in an elevated process); there is no macOS job since tauri-driver has no macOS support. The tauri-build job additionally runs the same probe headless and greps the report file for RENDER OK and -> 403.

scripts/check-wiki-links.js (npm run check:wiki, a step of scripts/ci.sh) is the GitHub wiki's missing build step: because a published wiki link that points nowhere is a silent dead end, it verifies for each of openwiki/ and user-guide/ that every internal link targets an existing page, every #section link targets an existing heading using GitHub's own anchor-slug rules (including duplicate-heading -1/-2 suffixes), every link leaving the bare-page-name form (images, ../-paths) resolves to a real file on disk, and every page is reachable from that directory's own table of contents (openwiki/_Sidebar.md, hand-maintained; user-guide/README.md's Guide contents). OKF YAML frontmatter is stripped before scanning so a frontmatter line is never mistaken for a heading or link; failures are listed and the script exits non-zero.

samples/git-scenarios is a rig of ready-made two-reviewer situations kept as definitions (scenarios.ts over base.ts) and built on demand into real repositories by `npm run scenario -- list | <name> [--out dir] | all --out dir | readme`; a built folder holds origin.git plus one clone per person (anna/, ben/). Builds are deterministic — fixed names, e-mails, a fixed commit clock one hour per tick, branch main, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM with an empty stand-in global config, hooks disabled and gpgsign off — and buildScenario refuses a non-empty --out folder or one inside any git working tree (including this repository) so a scenario's .git folders can never be committed by accident.

The scenario list in samples/git-scenarios/README.md is generated: `npm run scenario -- readme` prints scenariosMarkdown(), which must be pasted between the <!-- scenarios:begin --> / <!-- scenarios:end --> markers. gitScenarios.integration.test.tsx fails while they differ, builds every scenario and runs each definition's verify() — which drives SaiLoR's real mergeProjects over the built base/HEAD/origin revisions so a scenario someone opens by hand is known to show what its README entry claims — and additionally pins determinism (two builds of the same scenario give the same rev-parse HEAD) and the refuse-inside-a-work-tree guard.

Release installers are not gated by a test workflow: release.yml (triggered by a v* tag, workflow_dispatch, or a published release) does preflight checks, creates or finds a draft release, builds four targets via tauri-action with the release config and signed updater artifacts, checks latest.json lists all four platforms, and archives the published release on Zenodo — but runs no test suite. The test gates live entirely in ci.yml on pushes and pull requests.
